assignments.description: Capture the band that matched. Bands do not overlap, so at most one match occurs.
assignments.name: asgnCaptureBand
assignments.label: Capture Matching Band

assignments.description: BR-05: record the derived segment and the basis for it.
assignments.name: asgnSegmentResolved
assignments.label: Set Segment and Basis

assignments.description: BR-05: an employee count that matches no active band is surfaced, never defaulted to a segment.
assignments.name: asgnNoBandMatch
assignments.label: Set Unsegmentable - No Band

assignments.description: BR-05: never default an underivable segment. Missing employee count is stated, not guessed.
assignments.name: asgnNoEmployeeCount
assignments.label: Set Unsegmentable - No Employee Count

assignments.description: Count every Account sharing the normalized domain and capture its detail. Bands do not overlap; Accounts can, which is exactly what Review detects.
assignments.name: asgnCaptureAccount
assignments.label: Capture Candidate Account

assignments.description: BR-03. No Account shares this domain, or no domain was available.
assignments.name: asgnNoMatch
assignments.label: Set No Match

assignments.description: BR-03. Exactly one Account shares the normalized domain.
assignments.name: asgnMatched
assignments.label: Set Matched

assignments.description: BR-03/BR-13. Two or more Accounts share the domain. Never guess - surface for review.
assignments.name: asgnAmbiguous
assignments.label: Set Ambiguous Match

assignments.description: Account.Strategic_Account__c is the authoritative designation. A uniquely matched Strategic Account overrides the size-derived segment.
assignments.name: asgnStrategicSegment
assignments.label: Apply Strategic Designation

assignments.description: BR-06/BR-13. No country: territory cannot be derived. Never defaulted.
assignments.name: asgnMissingGeo
assignments.label: Set Missing Geography

assignments.description: A state-specific rule matched. Captured separately from country defaults so specificity - not record order - decides the winner.
assignments.name: asgnCaptureSpecific
assignments.label: Capture Specific Territory Rule

assignments.description: A country-default rule (blank State_Codes) matched. Used only if no state-specific rule matched.
assignments.name: asgnCaptureDefault
assignments.label: Capture Country Default Rule

assignments.description: BR-06. A state-specific rule beats the country default regardless of the order rules were returned in.
assignments.name: asgnTerritoryFromSpecific
assignments.label: Set Territory - Specific Rule

assignments.description: BR-06. No state-specific rule matched; the country default applies.
assignments.name: asgnTerritoryFromDefault
assignments.label: Set Territory - Country Default

assignments.description: BR-06/BR-13. Country present but covered by no active rule.
assignments.name: asgnUnsupportedGeo
assignments.label: Set Unsupported Geography

assignments.description: AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY BOUNDARY. Outside the governed intake path, ownership is preserved exactly as supplied or defaulted. This is NOT a routing exception - the Lead is not moved to the exception queue.
assignments.name: asgnNonRoutingIntake
assignments.label: Preserve Ownership - Non-Routing Intake

value.stringValue: Ownership preserved: record not received through governed intake

assignments.description: BR-07 tier 1. Strategic designation outranks everything else.
assignments.name: asgnOwnerStrategic
assignments.label: Assign Owner - Strategic Account

assignments.description: BR-07 tier 2. An existing customer goes to the Account owner, not a coverage pool.
assignments.name: asgnOwnerCustomer
assignments.label: Assign Owner - Existing Customer

assignments.description: BR-07 tier 3. Territory resolves to a coverage queue; several territories may share one.
assignments.name: asgnTargetTerritoryQueue
assignments.label: Target Territory Coverage Queue

assignments.description: BR-07 tier 4 and BR-13. Fail-safe terminal destination. A routing-eligible Lead is never left silently on its creator.
assignments.name: asgnTargetExceptionQueue
assignments.label: Target Routing Exception Queue

assignments.description: BR-08. Queue ownership plus the reason it was chosen.
assignments.name: asgnOwnerQueue
assignments.label: Assign Owner - Queue

assignments.description: BR-10 Stage A. Establishes the response deadline ONCE at intake. Write-once by construction: this element sits on the create path only, so no update can reach it and a later configuration change cannot retarget an existing Lead.
assignments.name: asgnSLATarget
assignments.label: Set SLA Target

assignments.description: BR-10. No deadline could be established. The target is left BLANK - never guessed - and the basis states why, so SLA_Status__c reads Unmeasurable or Excluded rather than silently absent.
assignments.name: asgnNoSLA
assignments.label: Record No SLA Established

assignments.description: BR-11 Stage B. Stamps first touch ONCE. The blank check in fxIsFirstTouch is the write-once guard, so repeated Status changes cannot move it.
assignments.name: asgnFirstTouch
assignments.label: Stamp First Touch

assignments.description: BR-15/PD-09. Creation IS entry into the initial lifecycle stage, so the timestamp is stamped once here rather than left null until the first transition. Without this a Lead sits in its first stage with no recorded entry time and the first computable duration would silently start at the wrong moment. It records when the record entered the stage IN THIS SYSTEM - a loaded record carries the load time, which is true and is not a claim about when the business event happened.
assignments.name: asgnStageEnteredOnCreate
assignments.label: Stamp Stage Entered - Creation

assignments.description: BR-17. Records WHY the Lead qualified, at the moment it qualified. Evidence only: it explains the decision and never defines it. Reached only after every required condition passed, so a blocked attempt can never leave a basis behind.
assignments.name: asgnMQLBasis
assignments.label: Capture MQL Qualification Basis

assignments.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Captures the acceptance event: WHEN it happened, WHO performed it from the authenticated identity, and WHY it was permitted. Reached only after every requirement the active policy declares has passed, so a refused attempt can never leave acceptance evidence behind. Sales_Accepted_At__c is separate from Lifecycle_Stage_Entered__c because that one is overwritten on the next transition and would stop answering when SAL was accepted the moment the Lead reaches SQL.
assignments.name: asgnSalesAcceptance
assignments.label: Capture Sales Acceptance Evidence

assignments.description: BR-15/BR-17. Records why SQL was permitted: the requirements the active policy declared and the values that satisfied them. Reached only after every declared requirement passed, so a refused attempt can never leave SQL evidence behind. Deliberately does NOT restate the Marketing or acceptance evidence - MQL_Basis__c and Sales_Acceptance_Basis__c still hold those, and the chain is read across the fields rather than copied into each one.
assignments.name: asgnSQLBasis
assignments.label: Capture SQL Qualification Basis

assignments.description: BR-15. The Lead has entered a new governed stage through a transition the policy allows, so the entry time moves. It moves ONLY here: an unrelated update never reaches this element, and a blocked transition never gets here either.
assignments.name: asgnStageEnteredOnTransition
assignments.label: Stamp Stage Entered - Allowed Transition

assignments.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Captures the rejection event: WHEN it happened, WHO declined it from the authenticated identity, and WHY it was permitted including the policy version in force. Reached only after every requirement passed, so a refused attempt can never leave evidence behind. OWNERSHIP IS NOT TOUCHED and neither is Status: the Lead remains MQL with its seller, because handing a declined Lead back to a queue is a routing decision that has not been governed.
assignments.name: asgnRejectionEvidence
assignments.label: Capture Sales Rejection Evidence

assignments.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Issues the seller-decision commitment at the moment MQL is granted. PERSISTED, NOT DERIVED: a formula field cannot follow the ACTIVE policy - Custom Metadata is reachable from a formula only by naming a record at authoring time - and pinning the deadline as issued means a later policy change cannot retroactively move a commitment already given. The time basis is the documented weekend-aware approximation, not Salesforce Business Hours.
assignments.name: asgnAcceptanceCommitment
assignments.label: Issue Seller Decision Commitment

customErrors.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Blocks entry into the governed accepted stage when Sales has not explicitly accepted, when the Marketing handoff it would be accepting is unsubstantiated, or when no individual owner is accountable for it. Names the requirements that were not satisfied without exposing field names. The whole save is rolled back: Status, the stage timestamp and all three acceptance evidence fields are left exactly as they were, and ownership is untouched - a refusal never reassigns the Lead.
customErrors.name: errSalesNotAccepted
customErrors.label: Block Unaccepted SAL Entry

customErrors.description: BR-15/BR-17. Blocks entry into the governed sales-qualified stage when the commercial qualification the policy requires has not been established. Names the requirements that were not satisfied without exposing field names. The whole save is rolled back: Status, the stage timestamp, SQL_Basis__c, the acceptance evidence and the Marketing evidence are all left exactly as they were.
customErrors.name: errSQLNotQualified
customErrors.label: Block Unqualified SQL Entry

customErrors.description: BR-17. Blocks entry into the governed qualified stage when the Lead has not earned it. Names the requirements that were not satisfied so an operator can act, without exposing field names or internal logic. The whole save is rolled back: Status, the stage timestamp and MQL_Basis__c are all left as they were.
customErrors.name: errMQLNotQualified
customErrors.label: Block Unqualified MQL Entry

customErrors.description: BR-15. Blocks a Lead save whose Status transition is absent from the governed policy. The whole save is rolled back, so Status and the stage timestamp are both left as they were. This element states no policy of its own - it only reports that the lookup found none.
customErrors.name: errInvalidLifecycleTransition
customErrors.label: Block Invalid Lifecycle Transition

customErrorMessages.errorMessage: This lifecycle transition is not allowed by the governed NorthstarIQ lifecycle policy: {!fxPriorStage} to {!fxNewStage}.

customErrors.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Blocks a Sales rejection the governed policy does not permit - no handoff to decline, no accountable individual owner, or a seller decision already recorded. The whole save is rolled back, so the reason is never left behind on the record without its evidence.
customErrors.name: errRejectionNotPermitted
customErrors.label: Block Ungoverned Sales Rejection

decisions.description: Segmentation requires an employee count. Absence is an explicit state, not a default.
decisions.name: decHasEmployeeCount
decisions.label: Has Employee Count?

decisions.description: BR-21: the band boundary test lives in configuration, not in this Flow.
decisions.name: decBandMatches
decisions.label: Band Matches Employee Count?

decisions.description: BR-03. Matching needs a normalized domain; without one there is nothing to match on.
decisions.name: decHasDomain
decisions.label: Has Normalized Domain?

decisions.description: BR-03. Exact equality on a normalized key. No fuzzy matching, no scoring.
decisions.name: decMatchCount
decisions.label: How Many Accounts Matched?

decisions.description: BR-06. CountryCode is a restricted standard picklist, so geography is already normalized.
decisions.name: decHasCountry
decisions.label: Has Country?

decisions.description: BR-21. Classifies each configured rule as state-specific or country-default. Specificity decides the winner after the loop, so correctness never depends on the order Custom Metadata is returned in.
decisions.name: decTerritoryRuleMatches
decisions.label: Classify Territory Rule

decisions.description: THE AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY BOUNDARY, and the CREATE / UPDATE seam. Automated ownership is authorized only for Leads entering through the governed NorthstarIQ Inbound intake path, and only at creation. On UPDATE the flow simply ends here: ownership and the original routing explanation are left untouched, which is what BR-08 AC5 requires. Owner state is never used to infer authorization - before-save automation cannot distinguish a defaulted owner from deliberate self-assignment.
decisions.name: decRoutingEligible
decisions.label: Routing Authority (Create Only)
decisions.defaultConnectorLabel: Update - Preserve Routing, Check First Touch

decisions.description: BR-07. Four explicit tiers, each consuming a structurally different business signal. First match wins.
decisions.name: decRoutingTier
decisions.label: Routing Precedence

decisions.description: BR-10. SLA eligibility. A routing-exception Lead is deliberately excluded: its next action is RevOps triage, not a seller response, and counting it as a seller breach would blame the wrong party.
decisions.name: decSLAEligible
decisions.label: SLA Eligible?

decisions.description: BR-11 Stage B. Runs on the UPDATE path only. Writes nothing except First_Touch_DateTime__c, and only when it is blank.
decisions.name: decFirstTouch
decisions.label: First Touch?

decisions.description: BR-15. Does this save involve a governed lifecycle event at all? Anything else - a name edit, a phone number, any update that leaves Status alone - takes the default path and never reaches the policy lookup, so an ordinary save costs nothing.
decisions.name: decLifecycleGate
decisions.label: Lifecycle Event?

rules.name: ruleStatusChanged
rules.label: Status changed on an existing Lead

decisions.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Did the lookup return an acceptance policy governing this stage? Only whether a record exists - no stage is named here. A stage with no active acceptance policy, or a policy that has been deactivated, takes the default path and is governed by the transition policy alone. This branch is reached only when the MQL gate did not apply, so the two gates stay separately readable rather than merging into one qualification branch.
decisions.name: decEnteringAcceptedStage
decisions.label: Entering the Governed Accepted Stage?

decisions.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Every requirement the ACTIVE ACCEPTANCE POLICY declares, none weighted. Status = SAL is the claim; these are the evidence. The Lead being at MQL is not treated as proof that Marketing legitimately qualified it - the substantiating MQL evidence is required separately, which is what stops an unsupported handoff being accepted by changing a picklist.
decisions.name: decSalesAccepted
decisions.label: Sales Acceptance Satisfied?

decisions.description: BR-15/BR-17. Did the lookup return an SQL policy governing this stage? Only whether a record exists - no stage is named here. Reached only when neither the MQL nor the SAL gate applied, so all three gates stay separately readable rather than merging into one generic qualification branch.
decisions.name: decEnteringSQLStage
decisions.label: Entering the Governed Sales-Qualified Stage?

decisions.description: BR-15/BR-17, PD-14. Every requirement the ACTIVE SQL POLICY declares, none weighted. SQL must prove something the prior stages did not: MQL proved Marketing had grounds to hand the Lead over, SAL proved Sales took it, and SQL proves Sales learned something FROM THE PROSPECT. Prior stages are consumed through their evidence and never re-tested here.
decisions.name: decSQLQualified
decisions.label: SQL Qualification Satisfied?

decisions.description: BR-17. Did the lookup return a policy governing this stage? The question is only whether a record exists - no stage is named here, so this Flow holds no copy of which stages require qualification. A stage with no active policy, or a policy that has been deactivated, takes the default path: entry falls back to transition governance alone rather than blocking every Lead.
decisions.name: decEnteringQualifiedStage
decisions.label: Entering the Governed Qualified Stage?

decisions.description: BR-17, PD-14. ALL required conditions, none weighted. There is no score, no threshold and no partial credit: a single unsatisfied condition means not qualified. Each condition is a separately named formula so an administrator can read the policy off the Flow one line at a time, and so the failure message and this test consume the SAME definition rather than two copies of it.
decisions.name: decMQLQualified
decisions.label: MQL Qualification Satisfied?

decisions.description: BR-15. Did the governed policy return a rule for this exact prior-to-new pair? The question is only whether a record exists. THE POLICY IS NOT RESTATED HERE - no stage name appears in any condition, so Lifecycle_Transition__mdt remains the single definition of what is allowed and this Flow holds no second copy of it.
decisions.name: decTransitionAllowed
decisions.label: Transition Allowed By Policy?

decisions.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Is a governed Sales rejection being recorded, and is it permitted? Placed where every path converges - create, lifecycle transition and plain update alike - because a rejection is not a Status change and would otherwise be reachable on a route that never checks it. Two rules evaluated in order: a permitted rejection is recorded, and any other claimed rejection is refused. A save claiming nothing simply passes through.
decisions.name: decSellerDecision
decisions.label: Governed Seller Rejection?

decisions.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Does this save owe a seller-decision commitment? True only when this transaction granted MQL and the active policy issues one. A policy carrying no acceptance hours issues nothing, so the capability sits dormant until the governing version declares it.
decisions.name: decMQLCommitment
decisions.label: Decision Commitment Owed?

Flow.description: BR-01, BR-03, BR-05, BR-06, BR-07, BR-08, BR-13. Normalizes the company domain and derives segment from governed Segment_Band__mdt configuration, recording the basis. Before-save: assigns fields on the triggering record only, performs no DML, and reads only Custom Metadata. Data quality remains the responsibility of the Data_Quality_Status__c and Data_Quality_Detail__c formula fields and is deliberately not duplicated here.

formulas.description: Source precedence: Website when present, otherwise the Email domain. Website and Email remain the unmodified provenance values.
formulas.name: fxRawDomain
formulas.expression: IF( NOT(ISBLANK({!$Record.Website})), LOWER(TRIM({!$Record.Website})), IF( AND(NOT(ISBLANK({!$Record.Email})), FIND("@", {!$Record.Email}) > 0), LOWER(TRIM(MID({!$Record.Email}, FIND("@", {!$Record.Email}) + 1, 255))), "" ) )

formulas.description: Strip the scheme. Applied before the www prefix so https://www. resolves in one pass.
formulas.name: fxNoProtocol

formulas.description: Strip a leading www. prefix only.
formulas.name: fxNoWww

formulas.description: BR-01: drop any path, query string or trailing slash, leaving the registrable domain.
formulas.name: fxNormalizedDomain

formulas.description: Inclusive lower bound, exclusive upper bound. A null Employee_Min excludes the band from size-based derivation, which is how Strategic is kept out of it. A null Employee_Max means no upper bound.
formulas.name: fxBandMatches

formulas.description: BR-05 explainability: concise, states the signal, the outcome and the rule version in force.
formulas.name: fxBasisResolved
fxBasisNoBand
formulas.expression: "Not segmentable: no active band matches employee count " & TEXT({!$Record.NumberOfEmployees})

formulas.description: BR-06. A state-specific rule: State_Codes is populated and the record's state appears in it. Comma padding stops CA matching inside CAN. First specific match wins.
formulas.name: fxRuleIsSpecificMatch

formulas.description: BR-06. A country-default rule: State_Codes is blank. Applied only when no state-specific rule matched.
formulas.name: fxRuleIsDefault

formulas.description: BR-07 tier 2. Account.Type carries Customer - Direct and Customer - Channel.
formulas.name: fxIsCustomer

formulas.description: Creation test used by the routing authority gate. Only a create may set ownership or stamp an intake classification.
formulas.name: fxIsNew

formulas.description: THE AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY TEST. Governed intake signal only. Never owner-state inference.
formulas.name: fxRoutingEligible
fxReasonStrategic
formulas.expression: "At intake: Strategic Account Owner: " & {!varAccountName} & " | Territory " & {!fxTerritoryLabel} & " | Rule v1.0"

formulas.name: fxReasonCustomer
formulas.expression: "At intake: Existing Customer Owner: " & {!varAccountName} & " | Territory " & {!fxTerritoryLabel} & " | Rule v1.0"

formulas.description: BR-08. Serves both the territory and the exception queue paths.
formulas.name: fxReasonQueue

formulas.description: BR-10. Eligible when a segment resolved, SLA hours are configured, and the Lead was not routed to the exception queue.
formulas.name: fxSLAEligible

formulas.description: Day of week of the intake moment. 0 = Sunday, 6 = Saturday.
formulas.name: fxNowDow

formulas.description: Weekend-aware start: a Lead arriving Saturday or Sunday starts its clock Monday.
formulas.name: fxStartAdj

formulas.description: APPROXIMATION - PORTFOLIO DEMO. Weekend-aware only. This is NOT Salesforce Business Hours and does NOT honour Holiday records; that remains a known production gap. The calculation is deliberately isolated in these five formulas so the basis can be replaced without touching any other element.
formulas.name: fxSLATarget

formulas.description: BR-08/BR-10 explainability: segment, configured hours, time basis and rule version in force at intake.
formulas.name: fxSLABasis

formulas.description: States why no deadline was established, so a blank target explains itself.
formulas.name: fxSLABasisNone

formulas.description: BR-11 write-once guard. The blank check is what stops a later Status change moving first touch.
formulas.name: fxIsFirstTouch
formulas.expression: AND( ISBLANK({!$Record.First_Touch_DateTime__c}), ISCHANGED({!$Record.Status}), OR( TEXT({!$Record.Status}) = "Working - Contacted", TEXT({!$Record.Status}) = "Closed - Converted", TEXT({!$Record.Status}) = "Closed - Not Converted" ) )

formulas.description: BR-15. Creation, distinguished from an update so the two lifecycle paths never mix.
formulas.name: fxIsNewLead

formulas.description: BR-15. A governed lifecycle transition is being attempted: an existing record, Status changed, and the two values genuinely differ. The last clause is not redundant - it keeps the policy lookup off a save where Status was touched without actually moving.
formulas.name: fxLifecycleTransitionAttempted

formulas.description: The stage being left. Feeds the policy lookup and the error message.
formulas.name: fxPriorStage

formulas.description: The Lead Source as text, so it can be compared against the governed source configuration.
formulas.name: fxMQLSourceValue

formulas.description: The derived segment as text, so it can be matched to its band.
formulas.name: fxMQLSegmentValue

formulas.description: CRITERION 1 - governed acquisition source. True when an active Routing_Readiness_Source__mdt record exists for this Lead Source. A purchased list or an unrecorded source returns nothing and fails.
formulas.name: fxMQLSourceGoverned

formulas.description: CRITERION 2 - routing readiness. A Lead is routing-ready when it resolved to a governed territory, so Sales coverage is already determined and the record is not bound for the routing exception queue. Reads the DERIVED value rather than re-testing CountryCode: Territory__c exists only because Routing_Rule__mdt mapped a present country, so the governed rule is consumed rather than copied. Data_Quality_Status__c would have been the more direct source, but Salesforce does not allow a formula field to be referenced in a before-save Flow - see the implementation log.
formulas.name: fxMQLRoutable

formulas.description: CRITERION 3 - segment eligible for qualification. Read from the segment band. An unsegmented Lead matches no band and fails, which is correct: a segment that was never derived cannot be declared eligible.
formulas.name: fxMQLSegmentEligible

formulas.description: CRITERION 4 - unambiguous account match. Ambiguity is the disqualifier, not absence: a Lead with no domain to match on was never evaluated and is not thereby suspect, while a Lead flagged Review would force Sales to re-establish ownership before acting.
formulas.name: fxMQLMatchUnambiguous

formulas.description: PD-14. Every requirement the ACTIVE POLICY DECLARES, none weighted. No points, no threshold, no partial credit - one unsatisfied requirement means not qualified. Each term is already policy-gated, so a requirement the policy does not declare evaluates true and drops out. The order is qualification eligibility first, then handoff readiness.
formulas.name: fxMQLQualified

formulas.description: BR-17. The explanation written to MQL_Basis__c, assembled from ONLY the requirements the active policy declares - so the evidence stays truthful when the policy changes and never claims a condition that was not tested. Carries the policy version, so a historical qualification stays interpretable after the definition moves on.
formulas.name: fxMQLBasisRaw
formulas.expression: "Qualified under MQL Policy " & {!getMQLPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & ": " & IF({!getMQLPolicy.Require_Governed_Source__c}, "governed source " & {!fxMQLSourceValue} & "; ", "") & IF({!getMQLPolicy.Require_MQL_Eligible_Segment__c}, {!fxMQLSegmentValue} & " segment eligible; ", "") & IF({!getMQLPolicy.Require_Routable_Territory__c}, "territory " & TEXT({!$Record.Territory__c}) & " resolved; ", "") & IF({!getMQLPolicy.Require_Unambiguous_Match__c}, "account match " & IF(ISBLANK(TEXT({!$Record.Match_Status__c})), "not evaluated", TEXT({!$Record.Match_Status__c})) & "; ", "")

formulas.description: BR-17. Trims the trailing separator left by the last declared requirement and holds the result inside the 255-character field.
formulas.name: fxMQLBasis

formulas.description: BR-17. Names the requirements that were not satisfied, built from the SAME criterion formulas the qualification test uses - so the message can never disagree with the decision, and a requirement the policy does not declare can never be reported as failed.
formulas.name: fxMQLFailureDetail
formulas.expression: "This Lead does not meet the governed NorthstarIQ MQL qualification requirements (MQL Policy " & {!getMQLPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & "). Not satisfied: " & IF({!fxMQLSourceGoverned}, "", "governed acquisition source; ") & IF({!fxMQLSegmentEligible}, "", "segment eligible for qualification; ") & IF({!fxMQLRoutable}, "", "resolved governed coverage; ") & IF({!fxMQLMatchUnambiguous}, "", "unambiguous account match; ")

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 1 - explicit Sales acceptance. Reads the seller INPUT field, which a human must deliberately tick. This is what stops acceptance being inferred from the Status change: moving to SAL without it is refused.
formulas.name: fxSALAcceptanceGiven

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 2 - substantiated Marketing handoff. An EVIDENCE-CHAIN check, deliberately NOT a re-evaluation: this gate never re-tests source, segment, coverage or match, so the MQL definition is not duplicated here. It asks only whether the Marketing claim carried evidence when it was made. Whether that evidence still holds is the business of the future detective control.
formulas.name: fxSALMQLEvidence

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 3 - an accountable individual owner. THE GOVERNED NORTHSTARIQ POLICY, NOT SALESFORCE BEHAVIOUR: Salesforce is perfectly willing to hold an accepted Lead on a queue, and this synthetic business decided it should not. A coverage queue is valid routing ownership before seller pickup; it is not an accountable person once SAL is claimed. Asks POSITIVELY whether the owner is a User, rather than whether it is not a queue - a Lead OwnerId is a User (005) or a Queue (00G), and a positive test refuses anything unexpected instead of admitting it. The key prefix is read straight off the record already in the transaction: no lookup, no formula field, no polymorphic Owner traversal, which a before-save Flow cannot rely on anyway. AN ACCOUNTABILITY CHECK, NOT A ROUTING RULE - this Flow never assigns ownership here, so the safeguard verifies that a seller took the Lead and never manufactures the accountability it is testing for.
formulas.name: fxSALOwnerAccountable

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Every requirement the active policy declares. No score, no threshold, no partial credit. Each term is policy-gated, so a requirement the policy does not declare evaluates true and drops out - which is why adding the third term changes nothing at all while Require_Individual_Owner__c is off.
formulas.name: fxSALAccepted

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. The explanation written to Sales_Acceptance_Basis__c, assembled from ONLY the requirements the active policy declares, so the evidence stays truthful when the policy changes. It describes the ACCEPTANCE decision; the Marketing claim it accepted stays in MQL_Basis__c and is never restated or overwritten here.
formulas.name: fxSALBasisRaw
formulas.expression: "Accepted under Sales Acceptance Policy " & {!getSALPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & ": " & IF({!getSALPolicy.Require_Explicit_Acceptance__c}, "explicit seller acceptance recorded; ", "") & IF({!getSALPolicy.Require_MQL_Evidence__c}, "Marketing handoff substantiated by MQL evidence; ", "") & IF({!getSALPolicy.Require_Individual_Owner__c}, "accountable individual owner in place; ", "")

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Trims the trailing separator left by the last declared requirement and holds the result inside the 255-character field.
formulas.name: fxSALBasis

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Names the requirements that were not satisfied, built from the SAME formulas the acceptance test uses - so the message can never disagree with the decision.
formulas.name: fxSALFailureDetail
formulas.expression: "This Lead cannot enter the governed NorthstarIQ Sales Acceptance stage (Sales Acceptance Policy " & {!getSALPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & "). Not satisfied: " & IF({!fxSALAcceptanceGiven}, "", "explicit Sales acceptance; ") & IF({!fxSALMQLEvidence}, "", "substantiated Marketing handoff evidence; ") & IF({!fxSALOwnerAccountable}, "", "an accountable individual owner - this Lead is still held by a queue, so no person has taken responsibility for it; ") & IF({!fxSALNoRejection}, "", "the absence of a Sales rejection - this handoff has been explicitly declined, and one Lead carries one governed seller decision; ")

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 1 - substantiated Sales acceptance. An EVIDENCE-CHAIN check against the immutable acceptance timestamp. The Sales Acceptance Policy is NOT re-run and the MQL policy is NOT re-run: a prior governed stage is consumed through its evidence, never re-tested.
formulas.name: fxSQLAcceptance

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 2 - confirmed business need. The picklist is RESTRICTED, so presence is sufficient here: Salesforce itself refuses any value outside the governed vocabulary, which is why this Flow does not restate the value list.
formulas.name: fxSQLNeed

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 3 - agreed forward motion. Date compared to Date: $Flow.CurrentDate, never $Flow.CurrentDateTime, so there is no Date/DateTime coercion. TODAY passes, a past date fails, a future date passes. This is a QUALIFICATION-TIME test - a date that was valid at entry will naturally fall into the past later, which is why a future detective control must judge against the recorded stage-entry evidence rather than against TODAY.
formulas.name: fxSQLNextStep

formulas.description: PD-14. Every requirement the active policy declares, none weighted. No points, no threshold, no partial credit. Each term is policy-gated, so a requirement the policy does not declare evaluates true and drops out.
formulas.name: fxSQLQualified

formulas.description: BR-15/BR-17. The explanation written to SQL_Basis__c, assembled from ONLY the requirements the active policy declares, so the evidence stays truthful when the policy changes. Records the need and the next-step date AS THEY WERE at qualification time, which is what makes the decision re-readable later.
formulas.name: fxSQLBasisRaw
formulas.expression: "Qualified under SQL Policy " & {!getSQLPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & ": " & IF({!getSQLPolicy.Require_Confirmed_Need__c}, "need " & TEXT({!$Record.Qualified_Need__c}) & "; ", "") & IF({!getSQLPolicy.Require_Next_Step__c}, "next step " & TEXT({!$Record.Next_Step_Date__c}) & "; ", "") & IF({!getSQLPolicy.Require_Acceptance_Evidence__c}, "substantiated Sales acceptance; ", "")

formulas.description: BR-15/BR-17. Trims the trailing separator left by the last declared requirement and holds the result inside the 255-character field.
formulas.name: fxSQLBasis

formulas.description: BR-15/BR-17. Names the requirements that were not satisfied, built from the SAME formulas the qualification test uses - so the message can never disagree with the decision.
formulas.name: fxSQLFailureDetail
formulas.expression: "This Lead does not meet the governed NorthstarIQ SQL qualification requirements (SQL Policy " & {!getSQLPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & "). Not satisfied: " & IF({!fxSQLNeed}, "", "confirmed business need; ") & IF({!fxSQLNextStep}, "", "agreed next step dated today or later; ") & IF({!fxSQLAcceptance}, "", "substantiated Sales acceptance; ")

formulas.description: The stage being entered. Feeds the policy lookup and the error message.
formulas.name: fxNewStage

formulas.description: The seller-decision deadline before the weekend shift. REUSES fxStartAdj - the same weekend-aware start already used for the response SLA - because that formula depends only on the transaction time, never on the response hours. Only the DURATION differs, so only the duration is restated here. Hours come from the active policy, never from this Flow.
formulas.name: fxAcceptRawTarget

formulas.description: APPROXIMATION - PORTFOLIO DEMO, stated in the same words as the response SLA it borrows the technique from. Weekend-aware only. This is NOT Salesforce Business Hours and does NOT honour Holiday records; that remains a known production gap requiring Apex. A deadline landing on a Saturday moves to Monday, and on a Sunday to Monday.
formulas.name: fxAcceptanceDue

formulas.description: Is a decision commitment owed on this save? Only when THIS transaction granted MQL - varMQLGranted is set on the qualification path and nowhere else, so no stage name is needed here - and only when the active policy actually issues one. A policy with no acceptance hours issues no commitment, which is how every version before v1.2 behaves and why activation stays reversible by policy succession alone.
formulas.name: fxCommitmentIssued

formulas.description: Is a rejection being claimed in THIS save? Populating the reason IS the act of rejecting, so no separate checkbox exists to disagree with it. Gated on the value actually changing, so an unrelated later edit to an already-rejected Lead does not re-run the decision or restamp its evidence. THE VALUE ITSELF IS NOT VALIDATED HERE - the picklist is RESTRICTED, so Salesforce refuses anything outside the governed vocabulary before this Flow ever sees it.
formulas.name: fxRejectionClaimed

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 1 - there is a handoff to decline. Expressed as the presence of the decision commitment rather than as a stage name, which keeps every lifecycle value out of this Flow and makes the test exact: a seller can only decline a handoff that was actually made to them.
formulas.name: fxRejectionInScope

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 2 - an accountable individual owner. THE SAME GOVERNED RULE AS ACCEPTANCE, read from the same policy record rather than restated: declining responsibility is as accountable an act as taking it, so a coverage queue can no more reject a handoff than accept one. Policy-gated, so switching the requirement off relaxes both halves together.
formulas.name: fxRejectionOwnerAccountable

formulas.description: REQUIREMENT 3 - no seller decision has already been made. One Lead carries one authoritative seller decision. Reversing a recorded decision is deliberately OUTSIDE MVP SCOPE: it would need its own authority and its own evidence, and half-building it here would leave a record that cannot explain itself.
formulas.name: fxNoPriorDecision

formulas.description: Every requirement a governed rejection declares. Same shape as fxSALAccepted, and policy-gated for the same reason.
formulas.name: fxRejectionPermitted

formulas.description: The mirror of fxNoPriorDecision on the acceptance side: acceptance cannot be granted while a rejection is claimed in the same save or already stands. Reads the REASON as well as the timestamp, because in a single save claiming both, the rejection stamp has not been written yet and only the incoming reason reveals the conflict.
formulas.name: fxSALNoRejection

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. The explanation written to Sales_Rejection_Basis__c: the reason given and the policy version in force. Carries the version because the NorthstarIQ version guard establishes which definition governed a record by reading it back out of the basis. EVIDENCE, NOT POLICY - and deliberately not an audit log: it explains one decision in one sentence.
formulas.name: fxRejectionBasis

formulas.description: Names the requirements a refused rejection did not satisfy, built from the SAME formulas the rejection test uses so the message can never disagree with the decision.
formulas.name: fxRejectionFailureDetail
formulas.expression: "This Lead cannot record a governed Sales rejection (Sales Acceptance Policy " & {!getDecisionPolicy.Policy_Version__c} & "). Not satisfied: " & IF({!fxRejectionInScope}, "", "a Marketing handoff to decline - no seller decision was ever requested on this Lead; ") & IF({!fxRejectionOwnerAccountable}, "", "an accountable individual owner - this Lead is still held by a queue, so no person can decline it; ") & IF({!fxNoPriorDecision}, "", "the absence of an earlier seller decision - this Lead already carries a governed acceptance or rejection, and reversing one is outside the governed process; ")

formulas.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. The evidence written beside the deadline: which acceptance policy issued the commitment, what target it declared, and the time basis that computed it. THE PROVENANCE HALF of the pinned deadline, exactly as SLA_Basis__c is for SLA_Target_DateTime__c - without it a deadline outlives the identity of the policy that set it, and an undecided Lead could only be explained by guessing at whichever version is active later. States the approximation honestly and claims no Business Hours or holiday precision. DESCRIBES THE COMMITMENT ONLY - it never asserts that a decision was made, which is the business of Sales_Acceptance_Basis__c and Sales_Rejection_Basis__c, neither of which overwrites this.
formulas.name: fxAcceptanceBasis

recordLookups.name: getActiveBands
recordLookups.label: Get Active Segment Bands

recordLookups.description: BR-03. Exact equality against the Account-side normalized domain formula.
recordLookups.name: getMatchingAccounts
recordLookups.label: Get Accounts By Normalized Domain

recordLookups.description: BR-06/BR-21. Territory mapping is configuration. Custom Metadata reads do not consume SOQL limits.
recordLookups.name: getTerritoryRules
recordLookups.label: Get Territory Rules For Country

recordLookups.description: Resolve the coverage queue DeveloperName held in configuration to its Group Id.
recordLookups.name: getQueue
recordLookups.label: Get Queue By Developer Name

recordLookups.description: BR-15, BR-16, PD-12. Is there an active acceptance policy governing THE STAGE BEING ENTERED? Filtering on Accepted_Stage__c keeps every stage name out of this Flow and makes selection deterministic - one active record per stage. Ordered by version descending so selection stays defined even if that convention were broken. Custom Metadata reads do not consume SOQL query limits. No fault connector by design - if the policy cannot be read the save fails rather than proceeding unvalidated.
recordLookups.name: getSALPolicy
recordLookups.label: Get Active Sales Acceptance Policy

recordLookups.description: BR-15/BR-17. Is there an active SQL qualification policy governing THE STAGE BEING ENTERED? Filtering on Qualified_Stage__c keeps every stage name out of this Flow and makes selection deterministic - one active record per stage. Ordered by version descending so selection stays defined even if that convention were broken. Custom Metadata reads do not consume SOQL query limits. No fault connector by design - if the policy cannot be read the save fails rather than proceeding unvalidated.
recordLookups.name: getSQLPolicy
recordLookups.label: Get Active SQL Qualification Policy

recordLookups.description: BR-17. Is there an active qualification policy governing THE STAGE BEING ENTERED? Filtering on Qualified_Stage__c is what keeps every stage name out of this Flow, makes selection deterministic - one active record per stage, so a later SAL or SQL policy cannot be picked up here by accident - and lets the same gate serve a future stage without a structural change. Ordered by version descending so selection stays defined even if the one-active-record convention were ever broken. Custom Metadata reads do not consume SOQL query limits. Runs on every allowed transition, not only on MQL ones, which is the cost of not naming a stage here. No fault connector by design - if the policy cannot be read the save fails rather than proceeding unvalidated.
recordLookups.name: getMQLPolicy
recordLookups.label: Get Active MQL Qualification Policy

recordLookups.description: BR-17/BR-02. Criterion 1: is this Lead Source one NorthstarIQ holds to a routing-readiness standard? The governed set is Routing_Readiness_Source__mdt, which the assessment already consumes - so the qualification policy and the assessment agree by construction rather than by coincidence. Custom Metadata read; no SOQL limit consumed.
recordLookups.name: getMQLSource
recordLookups.label: Get Governed Acquisition Source

recordLookups.description: BR-17/BR-05. Criterion 3: is the Lead's segment one the business qualifies? Eligibility lives on the band that already defines the segment, so there is one record per segment rather than a second type restating them. Custom Metadata read; no SOQL limit consumed.
recordLookups.name: getMQLSegmentBand
recordLookups.label: Get Segment Band For Eligibility

recordLookups.description: BR-15/BR-21. Asks the governed policy one question: is there an active rule for this exact prior-to-new pair? Custom Metadata reads do not consume SOQL query limits. One selective lookup, first record only - deliberately not a retrieve-all-and-loop, because a transition is exact equality rather than a range or a precedence contest. No fault connector by design: if the policy cannot be read the save fails rather than proceeding unvalidated.
recordLookups.name: getLifecycleTransition
recordLookups.label: Get Allowed Lifecycle Transition

recordLookups.description: The active Sales Acceptance policy, independent of any stage being entered. SEPARATE FROM getSALPolicy DELIBERATELY: that lookup selects by the stage the Lead is entering, which is correct when acceptance is granted but finds nothing at MQL entry, where the governing acceptance policy must still be read to issue its decision commitment. Filtered on Is_Active__c alone, exactly as the NorthstarIQ assessment queries it - the type only ever holds one active policy, so an active record IS the policy by construction and no stage name is needed. Custom Metadata, so no SOQL limit is consumed, and no loop encloses it.
recordLookups.name: getDecisionPolicy
recordLookups.label: Get Active Seller Decision Policy

variables.description: Set on the MQL qualification path and nowhere else, so the convergence point can tell that THIS transaction granted MQL without naming a lifecycle stage.
variables.name: varMQLGranted
